verdict.line: You lose trades and solo-kill chances levels 1-5 to Irelia's E-into-Q stun combo, but climb to a 51.3% win rate over 583 games once your Q is maxed and Shadowflame/Rabadon's come online.

brief.thesis: Irelia holds both lane advantage and solo-kill advantage because her E (Flawless Duet) stun chains directly into Q (Bladesurge) for a hard engage Gwen can't contest before she has E (Skip 'n Slash) and W (Hallowed Mist) up. Gwen's W only lets enemies who enter the mist target her, so the lane plan is to deny Irelia's dash windows rather than trade face to face. Her Q's true-damage center and %-health passive damage scale through Irelia's physical-damage kit, which is why the overall matchup is close to even despite a losing laning phase.

theirWindow.when: She has E and Q both up
theirWindow.what: Flawless Duet stuns anyone caught between the two converging blades and Marks them, letting Bladesurge dash in and refresh off the Mark; don't stand still near minion lines when both are available, especially levels 3-5 before your E attack-speed burst is strong enough to answer.

yourWindow.when: Her Q is on cooldown or whiffed
yourWindow.what: Bladesurge only refreshes if the target is Marked or dies, so if she dashes a minion and whiffs, her main engage/escape tool is down for up to 10 seconds early, 6 at rank 5; drop W, walk up, and punish with Q's true-damage center before she has it back.

start.why: The 51.6% win rate, 83.6%-pick start over 597 games gives mana for repeated Q pokes and two potions to offset Irelia's early all-in damage without a back.

boots.why: 63% pick, 52.1% win rate — Irelia's damage comes from physical autos and on-hit stacks off Ionian Fervor, so flat armor directly cuts her all-in and extended-trade damage.

core.why: First item in the 62%-win-rate, 31.8%-pick path; builds your %-health passive damage early so trades start scaling in your favor around level 9.
Second in the same build path; the burst bonus against lower-health targets pairs with your passive and Q true damage to punish Irelia once she's been chunked.
Completes the 121-game, 62% win-rate core; raw AP scaling turns your %-health passive and R casts into the main source of damage late.

situational.when: the game goes long and you need sustain through extended skirmishes with irelia
irelia or her team starts stacking magic resist to blunt your passive and q damage
you're already ahead and want to prioritize magic penetration over the armor from steelcaps
irelia's q heal and her team's sustain are keeping her in lane through your trades

runes.keystoneWhy: The 47.5%-win-rate, 33.4%-pick page runs Conqueror because Gwen's trades are extended melee skirmishes, not single bursts, and the stacking adaptive damage plus healing lets her out-sustain Irelia's Bladesurge self-heal in a prolonged fight.

summoners.why: Flash+Ignite is both the highest pick rate (63.8%) and win rate (52.1%) combo, giving you kill pressure for the windows when Irelia's Q is down or she commits a Bladesurge into your W mist. If you're getting all-in'd repeatedly before level 6, Exhaust+Flash (52.5% over 8.6% pick) is the measured defensive alternative to survive the E-into-Q combo.

playing.title: Hold W for the dash
playing.detail: Enemies can only target you once they enter the mist from W (Hallowed Mist), so drop it before Irelia commits Q or E rather than after — force her to walk in and eat your Q's true-damage center.

playing.title: Respect the level 3 all-in
playing.detail: Once Irelia has E (Flawless Duet) to stun between her converging blades and Q (Bladesurge) to stick, she can chain a full combo; don't stand in minion-dash range without W up until you have E for the attack-speed/magic on-hit answer.

playing.title: Walk through her, not around
playing.detail: Q (Snip Snip!) only deals true damage and applies your passive to units in the center of the cone, not the outer snips, so path directly through Irelia rather than clipping the edge of the cone.

playing.title: Punish a whiffed Bladesurge
playing.detail: Q only refreshes if her target is Marked or dies; if she dashes a minion and misses you, her engage/escape is down for up to 10 seconds early (6s at rank 5) — that's your cue to E (Skip 'n Slash) in.

playing.title: Ignore her W charge
playing.detail: Defiant Dance only reduces physical damage taken, and your damage is almost entirely magic or true (passive, Q, E on-hit, R), so don't back off a trade just because she's charging it.

playing.title: Trade ultimates, not lives
playing.detail: Both ultimates are on long cooldowns at rank 1 — your R (Needlework) at 120s, her R (Vanguard's Edge) at 125s — so if she burns hers to force a fight, you can safely shove with your up to three R casts and reset the wave.

playing.title: Play for level 9, not level 3
playing.detail: Your head-to-head win rate (51.3% over 583 games) comes from scaling, not early trading; farm through the losing lane phase and let maxed Q plus Dusk and Dawn into Shadowflame and Rabadon's flip the matchup.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, boots, runes, summoners and the win-rate figures above are measured from live games on the current patch (OP.GG); the mechanical reasoning — why the all-in windows, the W timing, and the scaling crossover happen — is my own tactical read, not sourced data.
